text:
alex: Quick heads-up — planning to move prod SIEM export retention from 180d -> 90d for hot indices to reduce costs. Need to confirm: who should retain access to full raw exports after the cutover? @maria @jordan

maria: I support shorter hot retention, but we need a clear JIT flow for analysts + audit team. We can't break incident repro. :thinking_face:

jordan: For external auditors we should use timeboxed exports with CMK unwrap that logs who requested keys. No permanent read role.

eve: +1. Proposal: short retention for standard exports, longer cold archive in GCS with stricter KMS wrap, and a request-for-export ticket template.

alex: Good. Draft of the export ticket template I had in mind:```
Title: SIEM export request — <reason>
Duration: <24h | 72h | other>
Data scope: <indices / tenant>
Reviewer: <security oncall>
CMK unwrap: <required yes/no>
```
Keep it minimal.

maria: Also: RBAC change needed — remove broad "siem_reader" from platform-admin role. Create two roles: "siem_query" (no export) and "siem_exporter" (export by approval).

jordan: How do we audit exporter actions? We should have an immutable audit log entry when a CMK is unwrapped and include ticket id. security-bot: recorded KMS unwrap event -> key_id=projects/keys/rlw-prod-keys/1234, actor=jordan, ticket=INC-4521

eve: Can we do automatic stamping in the export pipeline? If ticket ID present, the pipeline should inject metadata and copy to archive bucket with server-side encryption CMK.

alex: Ops question: do we rotate the CMK monthly or on demand? Rotation affects ability to re-decrypt older archive snapshots.

maria: Rotate annually and provide key-rotation metadata in the archive manifest. For re-decrypting old archives we require a key escrow process that passes audit review.

jordan: Example gating flow I propose:
1) Request ticket created with selectors + justification
2) Security oncall reviews & approves in 3 business hours
3) approver invokes KMS unwrap with ephemeral grant (logged)
4) Export pipeline stamps ticket id and exporter id, uploads to archive (CMK wrap)
5) Post-mortem entry created in case of sensitive data found

alex: Nice. Two open questions: A) Who gets permanent access to cold archives? B) How long do we keep the manifests?

eve: A) Only legal + designated forensics group + security SRE lead. Access via privileged request and short-lived IAM bindings. B) Keep manifests for 7 years for compliance, but keep minimal PII in manifest.

maria: Implementation notes:
- Add Terraform module for export role with time-limited binding
- Add Cloud Function to ingest ticket metadata and stamp exports
- Add OPA policy to block exports without ticket id

alex: Can eng-infra help with the TF module? @jordan FYI to pick up the Cloud Function patch.

jordan: I'll pick the Cloud Function and OPA rule. Plan to submit PR tomorrow.

sre-bot: deploy job queued: export-pipeline-stamp-service v0.3.1 -> staging

alex: Action items summarized:
- maria: finalize RBAC role definitions + policy snippets (due EOD)
- jordan: PR for stamp service + OPA rule (submit tomorrow)
- eve: draft ticket template + archive access runbook (next week)
- security: confirm CMK rotation cadence and escrow process docs

security-bot: reminder: any KMS unwrap must include ticket id or will be denied by policy.

alex: Thanks everyone — let's sync in the oncall huddle if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
